sections.html:
Pullman is a college town in the Palouse, in eastern Whitman County about 65 miles south of Spokane and 32 miles north of Lewiston, Idaho. On July 1, 2025 the estimate stood at 33,756 residents, 2.6% above April 2020. Washington State University is the reason most buyers and renters come.

Selling here usually means thinking about two kinds of buyer: families who want to stay, and investors who want a student rental. Registering and licensing a rental, covered below, matter to that second group.

About two of every three Pullman homes are rented. Just 32.0 percent of homes are owner-occupied (2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied home is valued at $424,800 and median gross rent is $1,062. There are 12,682 households of 2.07 people on average, with a median income of $46,812. A mere 65.6% of residents stayed in the same house for a year, which shows how much of the market turns over with the school year. Pricing works better from nearby sales of comparable houses than from the citywide median.

Owners of residential rental property must register with the City of Pullman under Pullman City Code 6.98. The Police Department's permits and licenses page names the Code Enforcement Supervisor, at 509-334-0802, for questions. Short-term rentals follow a separate process under chapter 17.109, with application instructions that spell out what an owner submits.

RequirementCost or detail
Rental registration (code 6.98)One-time $15 per address
Short-term rental fee$200, paid before review starts
Business licenseNAICS code 721199, applied for before final approval
Insurance and liability coverageAs required by RCW 64.37.050

A short-term rental application also needs a floor plan showing beds, smoke and carbon monoxide detectors, fire extinguishers and an emergency egress light, plus an evacuation plan and a plot plan showing off-street parking. Approval can carry an occupancy limit of the number of sleeping rooms plus two. If your house runs as a rental, tell a buyer which registrations are current and hand over the paperwork.

Pullman sits across four hills of windblown loess: Military Hill, Pioneer Hill, Sunnyside Hill and College Hill. Downtown lies in a valley where Missouri Flat Creek and Paradise Creek join the South Fork of the Palouse River. Steep lots and drainage are worth documenting if your house sits on a slope.

Winters are cold and wet and summers hot and dry. The building division's design criteria include a ground snow load of 30 pounds per square foot, a frost depth of 30 inches and a required ice barrier underlayment on roofs. Pullman adopted the 2021 International Building and Residential Codes, effective March 15, 2024.

Reroofing, residing and replacement windows often need no plan review, and the city can issue those permits online, over the counter or next day. Projects that change the structure or footprint go through plan review that can take four to six weeks. Email applications to pwcd-admin@pullman-wa.gov, or visit 190 SE Crestview Street, Building A. Close any open permit before listing, since a buyer's lender or inspector may raise it.

The Pullman School District covers Franklin, Jefferson, Sunnyside and Kamiak elementary schools, Lincoln Middle School and Pullman High School, the city's only public high school. U.S. Route 195 and State Route 27 run north toward Spokane, US 195 also runs south to Lewiston, and State Route 270 connects Pullman with Moscow, Idaho. Pullman Transit serves residents and WSU students. Mean travel time to work is 14.6 minutes, a short commute that is part of the appeal. If your house is close to campus or a bus line, say so in the listing, and name the school it feeds, since families look at that early. Pullman High is on Military Hill, and students can take Running Start courses through WSU and Spokane Falls Community College.

sections.h2: Excise tax on a Pullman sale
sections.html:
RCW 82.45.080 puts this tax on the seller. The state rate runs from 1.1% on the first slice to 3% on the highest, with a local portion added, and the Whitman County Treasurer knows which local rate applies in the city. The first band ends at $525,000 now. Sales beginning January 1, 2027 have breakpoints of $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Notarization of the deed decides which set applies, so a closing signed in late December uses the 2026 numbers.

The Whitman County Treasurer handles real estate excise tax, so the affidavit, deed and payment go to its office at 400 N Main Street in Colfax. If the seller leaves it unpaid, a lien can attach and the buyer may become responsible.

sections.h2: Whitman County property taxes at closing
sections.html:
Two payment dates, April 30 and October 31, come from RCW 84.56.020, and a bill of $50 or less is paid whole by April 30. Call the Treasurer to confirm which schedule your parcel follows.

  • Treasurer: 400 N Main Street, Colfax, mailing address P.O. Box 550, phone 509-397-6230.
  • Office hours: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m.
  • Ask your closing officer to prorate the year and clear any unpaid half from sale proceeds.

Ask the Whitman County Assessor whether a senior, disability or other reduction applies to your parcel, and ask the Treasurer how the year's tax will be split at the closing table. Behind on taxes? Phone the Treasurer first, ahead of listing.

Before a buyer or investor visits, assemble what they will ask for. Bring your deed, the latest Whitman County tax statement and any payoff letter. If the house has been a rental, add the city registration, current leases and any short-term rental approval. Add permit records for reroofing, residing or window replacement, since the city issues those quickly and a buyer may want proof. For work on a slope, include drainage notes or a survey.

When the buyer is ready, the title company or closing officer drafts a settlement statement, you sign the deed and affidavit, and the Treasurer receives the tax. A cash sale usually moves faster because there is no lender to satisfy, but the documents are the same.

Pullman owners can list, sell privately, or accept an as-is offer in cash. Deed and excise tax steps match across all three.

  • A listing does best when the timing fits the academic calendar and the house shows well.
  • An investor purchase suits a rental with tenants, deferred repairs or a lease that ends mid-year.
  • Quiz each buyer on tenant notice, registration records and the closing date.

For a rented house, gather the leases, the registration confirmation and any short-term rental approval before you speak to a buyer. Tenants usually care about the dates, and a buyer will price in whatever turnover they expect. If the house is owner-occupied, the school year may shape the best time to show it, since families tend to shop around it. Sorting these facts first shortens the conversation with every buyer, whether you list or sell directly.

faqs.q: What is the owner-occupied rate in Pullman?
faqs.a: For 2020 to 2024 it was 32.0%, so roughly two of every three occupied homes are rented. Many buyers will be investors or will ask for rental history.

faqs.q: Must a Pullman rental house be registered?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners of residential rental property register with the city under Pullman City Code 6.98, paying a one-time $15 per address.

faqs.q: What does a Pullman short-term rental application cost?
faqs.a: The application instructions list a $200 short-term rental fee, paid before review begins. You also need a business license under NAICS code 721199 and the insurance that RCW 64.37.050 requires.

faqs.q: How long does a Pullman building permit take?
faqs.a: Reroofing, residing and window replacement may be issued online, over the counter or next day. More involved projects take four to six weeks for plan review.

faqs.q: Where does the Pullman excise tax go?
faqs.a: The Whitman County Treasurer, in Colfax, since the payment goes to the county where the property is. The seller owes it under RCW 82.45.080.
